title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', Grothendieck tests the defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations) in a linear model. The free profinite group is replaced by GL(2), or more generally by a form G of GL(2) attached to an Azumaya algebra M over S = Spec A. The two elliptic generators of SL(2,Z) are ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (characteristic polynomial x²−x+1, order 6) and σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (x²+1, order 4).

This page closes the 'cas général' study of the equation [β,σ] = η, then states a summarising Proposition for both equations
  [α,ρ] = α ρ(α)⁻¹ = ξ  and  [β,σ] = β σ(β)⁻¹ = η,
where ρ(α) means ρ α ρ⁻¹. The unknowns α, β lie in GL(2,A), with A = Z, Z_ℓ or Ẑ.

Necessary conditions. Since ξρ = αρα⁻¹, it is conjugate to ρ, so det ξ = 1 and Tr(ξρ) = 1. Likewise ησ = βσβ⁻¹ gives det η = 1 and Tr(ησ) = 0. With ησ = [[S,-R],[U,-T]], the second condition reads S = T: η must be symmetric.

Proposition, part 1. A solution exists iff ξρ (resp. ησ) is 'regular', i.e. on no fibre is it scalar. Equivalently, A² is an invertible module over A[ρ] = A[ζ6] (resp. A[i]). Over Z this is a Latimer–MacDuffee argument: Z[ζ6] and Z[i] have class number 1, so every cyclic module is free and hence conjugate to ρ (resp. σ).
- The characteristic polynomial can have a repeated root only mod 3 (resp. mod 2), so non-regularity can only occur there.
- The next page adds a sufficient condition: D (resp. U) is a unit, since the corresponding entry of ρ⁻¹ (resp. σ⁻¹) is 0.

Part 2. Solutions are unique up to right multiplication by the centraliser A[ρ]* (resp. A[i]*). Hence det α is defined modulo norms, and the obstruction to a solution of determinant 1 lies in A*/N(A[ρ]*) (resp. A*/N(A[i]*)). Over Z this group is ±1.

Part 3 (finished on the next page). An SL(2,A) solution exists iff D ≡ 1 mod 3 (resp. U ≡ 1 mod 4).
- Reason: from (31), (rt−su)·U = t²+u² = N(tσ+u), a norm from Z[i] that is odd, hence ≡ 1 mod 4. So det β ≡ U mod 4.
- Similarly the norm form t²−tu+u² of Z[ζ6] is never ≡ 2 mod 3.
- This is the content of the margin note 'en fait ≡ 1 (4)': the residue of U mod 4 is a priori ±1, but must equal 1 for an SL₂ solution.
- Over Z_ℓ with ℓ ≠ 3 (resp. ℓ ≠ 2) the condition is automatic, because every ℓ-adic unit is a norm of a unit from the unramified or split quadratic extension.

The page thus serves as a lemma toward equation (32), [α,ρ] = [β,σ]·ε₁(μ−1), the linear analogue of a GT-type relation coupling the two elliptic 'lacets' through a one-parameter subgroup ε₁ : G_a → SG.
errors: With ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] as written, ξρ = [[-B, A+B],[-D, C+D]] has trace C + D − B. The trace condition should therefore read C + D − B = 1, not 'B + D − C = 1' as written in (16). This is either a slip or a sign convention from earlier pages not visible here.
The word 'singulière' is surely 'régulière'. The condition is that ξρ (resp. ησ) be NON-scalar on every fibre, as the next page confirms ('sur aucune fibre ... ne soit un multiple scalaire').

Minor: 'Tr(ησ) = Tr σ' (previous page) is correct, but for ρ the corresponding condition Tr(ξρ) = Tr ρ = 1 is not restated explicitly. The resulting equation (16) appears to have a sign inconsistency with the displayed ξρ.

ideas.what: Solvability of the commutator equation [α,ρ] = ξ is equivalent to conjugacy of ξρ to ρ. This is classified by regularity (cyclicity) plus the class group of Z[ζ6], resp. Z[i] (trivial).
ideas.modern_name: Latimer–MacDuffee correspondence / conjugacy classes of elliptic elements in GL2(Z)

ideas.what: The obstruction to a determinant-one solution is A*/N(A[ρ]*). It is detected by D mod 3 (resp. U mod 4), and vanishes ℓ-adically for ℓ ≠ 3 (resp. ℓ ≠ 2).
ideas.modern_name: norm-residue obstruction; local norm groups of unramified vs. ramified quadratic extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (local class field theory / elementary number theory)

ideas.what: A linear (GL2 / Azumaya-form) model of the GT 'lacet' relations, using the order-4 and order-6 elliptic elements of SL2(Z) and a one-parameter subgroup ε₁ (developed on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: testing Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations in linear representations of the braid/modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completions) for linear/representation shadows

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a systematic study of GT-type relations ('équation des lacets') with values in forms of GL(2) over Z, Z_ℓ, Ẑ given by Azumaya algebras. Here he solves the individual commutator equations completely, including integral and ℓ-adic SL2 obstructions. This linear-algebraic toy model of GT does not appear as such in the literature.
missed.quote: Pour qu'il y ait une solution dans Sl(2,A), il faut et suffit qu'on ait D ≡ 1 (3) (resp. U ≡ 1 (4))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Low-dimensional 'linearised' shadows of the GT relations, over arithmetic rings rather than over fields, could give explicit test cases for GT actions on SL2-character varieties. The mathematics on this page itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but classical computation: conjugacy of elliptic elements in GL2 over Z, Z_ℓ, Ẑ and the norm obstructions mod 3 and mod 4. It is interesting only as part of an unpublished linear model of the GT relations; the results themselves are routine.
transcription_corrections: 'singulière, i.e. un scalaire mod un quelconque' should read roughly 'régulière, i.e. non scalaire sur aucune fibre'.
Margin note: 'en fait ≡ 1 (1)' should be 'en fait ≡ 1 (4)'.
'[α,ρ] = αρ(αρ)⁻¹' should be '[α,ρ] = αρ(α)⁻¹', where ρ(α) denotes conjugation by ρ.
'la racine de U mod 4' is likely 'la classe (or le résidu) de U mod 4'.
Opening line: 'on sait comme d'habitude que U est inversible ...' rather than 'comme d'ailleurs'.
'(dans Z, ou même Z_ℓ)' — the insertion reads 'même'.
